messages:

Subject: Unplanned preemption during demo window — urgent ask about eviction policy

Sofia / Marissa,

Quick note from this morning's customer demo — we had a hard preemption in the middle of a live walkthrough. The app dropped to degraded latency for ~45s while the request retried against a fallback model. That was visible to the customer and cost us the narrative in the call.

We are under the 12-month pilot (DEAL-3472) and had explicitly asked for predictable throughput during demos and spikes. We understand fleet pressure, but we need a clear contract-level protection for at least a 3-hour demo window when requested, and transparency about what triggers eviction.

Can you confirm:
- What eviction tiers exist today (reserved, soft-reserve, preemptible)?
- Notification SLA when a deal is about to be preempted?
- Options for a short-term reserved lane for demos (range in GPUs, cost delta)?

I'm attaching session logs from the demo (session_logs.zip) so you can see the timing. Our renewal decision is influenced by whether demos are reliable. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Sanjay Verma
Head of Platform
HelixAI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sanjay Verma <sanjay@helixai.com>
Date: 2028-04-28T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Unplanned preemption during demo window — urgent ask about eviction policy

Sofia — thanks, reviewing now. Quick summary of what happened and a proposed operational guardrail:  

What we saw: preemption was triggered by a transient burst across multiple deals in the same pool; Helix's requests were running at a standard (non-quantized) model variant and were matched to a pooled slot without a deal-specific reservation. When the autoscaler reclaimed capacity to meet a short-lived sustained throughput, existing non-reserved requests were preempted in LIFO order.

Proposal (short term, operational):
- Temporary soft-reservation: allocate a 4-GPU soft-reserved tranche for Helix for up to 7 days. Soft-reserved = capacity is logically reserved but can be preempted by emergency SLA exceptions; preemption will follow a 10-minute warning window and an automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized model variant for degraded latency instead of outright fail.
- Notification: 2-minute and 10-minute preemption notices via webhook + email for customer-facing sessions identified in advance.
- Cost delta: soft-reservation premium = +22% on the token unit price during reservation hours. We'll provide a detailed breakdown in the capacity_plan_v2.xlsx attached.
- Escalation: if Helix experiences >3 visible preemptions in a rolling 30-day window, the account escalates to the Capacity Committee for a potential hard reservation and credits back to the customer for impacted demo windows.

Proposal (medium term, contract change):
- Introduce a deal-level eviction SLA clause: scheduled demo protection windows (customer-initiated) up to X hours per quarter with defined notification and credit mechanics. Draft attached: redwood_sla_draft.pdf.

Next steps:
- Sofia to confirm customer approval of the short-term lane (Sanjay) and whether they want us to schedule the lane for upcoming demo windows.
- I'll provision the soft-reserved tranche pending confirmation and tag the capacity with DEAL-3472 to track usage.
